hyps.why: Replacing a parameter-free skip with a 3x3 conv gains much more than replacing a conv_1x1 or avg_pool (runs 3, 6 vs 7, 1).
Swapping a skip for a 3x3 conv adds learnable capacity, giving larger gains than edits where the edge already holds a conv or none (runs 13, 15).
Upgrading a skip on edge 4 to a 3x3 conv helps more than changing a none or conv_1x1 edge (runs 43, 46 vs 45, 49, 50).
Replacing a pooling edge into the output with a 3x3 conv yields a larger gain than replacing a conv or skip (runs 54, 59 vs 51, 60).
Replacing an avg_pool on edge 2 with a conv_1x1 is a bigger upgrade than editing a cell where edge 2 is already a 3x3 conv (runs 94, 96 vs 91, 95).
Removing a weak avg_pool direct edge costs little or even helps, unlike removing a conv edge (runs 64, 65 vs 61, 68).
Deleting the direct input-to-output edge hurts when it is a 3x3 conv, especially on ImageNet16 (runs 61, 68).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the output-feeding edge with pooling loses the most useful op, hurting all three datasets (runs 81, 85, 88, 90).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 2 with a skip loses capacity and consistently hurts (runs 21, 27).
Adding a 3x3 conv where edge 0 was absent opens the input-to-node-1 path and gains more than tweaking an existing conv edge (runs 5, 9 vs 7, 8).
